name: Ganesh Infraworld Limited
sector: EPC, water infrastructure, mining operations and transportation
summary: Ganesh Infraworld is a rapidly scaled EPC contractor that has added mining, transportation and equipment leasing. The strongest evidence is substantial parent-level revenue and operating-profit expansion; the decisive weakness is repeated operating cash outflow followed by a much larger acquired debt/asset perimeter. At ₹84, a roughly 4.99x parent TTM earnings cross-check looks optically inexpensive, but does not establish the value of the enlarged group. This is a funding-sensitive special situation, not an evidence-backed compounder. Current-group incremental returns and financeable equity returns remain NS. Restrained no-rescue models fail after a modeled, unverified October bridge, so the funding gate excludes a favorable new-purchase conclusion. Observed current liquidity, committed funding, actual collections and attributable subsidiary economics could materially change that assessment. No actual default or proven misconduct is alleged. [S1][S2][S9][S10][S17]
identity_note: Listed SME security and capital verified against issuer filings and ISIN-matched NSE market/master data; former Ganesh International partnership succeeded by the company in February 2024. [S7][S8][S16][S18]

quote.kind: Official close; not live executable quote

score_note: BQS/GQS/IAS NS due factor-specific CAP/R/P gaps; 88%/85%/30% coverage. Persistent CASH weakness implies GQS cap5; conditional modeled G3 failure implies IAS cap3. Missing scores stay NS.

gates.reason: No substantiated severe diversion or minority abuse established from reviewed records. Related-party capital allocation and dated disclosure-control issues warrant caution. An ED search is not a finding of wrongdoing; the company response must accompany it.

Signed annual and limited-review statements support bounded analysis. March accounting control reconciles the main group-perimeter issue; XBRL period tagging was acknowledged. Legacy prospectus cash-flow narrative conflicts are reconciled to the signed annexure. Current residual attribution and granular historical IC remain gaps, not evidence of missing cash.

Conditional model gate failure, not observed default: after an unverified October bridge, flat-growth/no-rescue essential-operation cases reach absolute cash deficits. Base-margin halt-growth fails by ₹5.17 lakh in November; restrained margins fail by ₹375.83 lakh, even with demand renewal. Small timing-sensitive deficits and estimated maintenance mean the exact dates are not predictions. Verified October liquidity or committed funding could change this gate. IAS cap 3 applies but IAS remains NS.

Eligible SM series and trades in all 60 sampled sessions; historical reference exit capacity is 1.96 days at 5%, versus 2.88 days using recent 20-session turnover. Lot 800 and sparse-participant/irregular-trading cautions matter. Neither status 6 nor those alerts establishes suspension.

sections.title: 1. Executive Verdict
sections.text: Ganesh Infraworld is a rapidly scaled EPC contractor that has added mining, transportation and equipment leasing. The strongest evidence is substantial parent-level revenue and operating-profit expansion; the decisive weakness is repeated operating cash outflow followed by a much larger acquired debt/asset perimeter. At ₹84, a roughly 4.99x parent TTM earnings cross-check looks optically inexpensive, but does not establish the value of the enlarged group. This is a funding-sensitive special situation, not an evidence-backed compounder. Current-group incremental returns and financeable equity returns remain NS. Restrained no-rescue models fail after a modeled, unverified October bridge, so the funding gate excludes a favorable new-purchase conclusion. Observed current liquidity, committed funding, actual collections and attributable subsidiary economics could materially change that assessment. No actual default or proven misconduct is alleged. [S1][S2][S9][S10][S17]

sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Ganesh Infraworld Limited; NSE SME, GANESHIN, ISIN INE0TVT01024. Research cutoff 20 October 2026, India; last market-session close ₹84 on 19 October. Issued shares 43,770,997 imply market capitalization ₹367.68 crore. Remaining 4,183,200 warrants would increase shares to 47,954,197 before any hypothetical rescue issuance. Five-year horizon ends 20 October 2031; assumed equity hurdle 15% nominal, before personal tax; ₹5 lakh is only the liquidity-test reference. Financial sources use INR lakh; narrative uses crore unless stated. [S6][S7][S8][S17]

Accounts follow Indian GAAP Accounting Standards (AS), including AS 21/AS 23 under the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, not an assumed Ind AS basis. Consolidated accounts describe investable group obligations; comparable parent/predecessor history is used where first-time KTL consolidation distorts growth and returns. G1 and G2 are Conditional, G3 fails the stated conditional stress model, G4 is Conditional. Historical claim-table confidence is High; predecessor comparability, governance and cash conversion are Medium; current-group incremental capital returns and financeable valuation inputs are Low. Overall investment-conclusion confidence is Low because the weakest material funding/attribution inputs cannot be averaged away. [S1][S2][S3]

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
BQS, GQS and IAS are NS, not zero, neutral scores or renormalized composites. Factors: GOV 5, MOAT 4, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP NS, CASH 2, BAL 3, EXEC 5, EARN 6; IAS factors R NS, D 2, P NS and L 7. BQS has 88% factor-weight coverage and GQS 85%; their exact known contributions and mathematical missing-factor bounds are in the score audit. IAS coverage is 30% because BQS/Q, R and P are unavailable. [S1][S2][S16]

REV starts at 9 from the 84.02% FY23-FY26 standalone/predecessor CAGR and is capped at 8 for Medium confidence and a shorter relevant history. No one-quarter adjustment is applied. Persistent CASH 2 triggers a GQS ceiling of 5; modeled G3 failure triggers an IAS ceiling of 3. Neither ceiling becomes a score when a critical factor is NS. An assumed 42.40% base IRR must not be converted to R 10. A one-point change in MOAT changes BQS known contribution by 0.20; one point in DUR changes BQS by 0.10 and GQS by 0.20. These are judgment sensitivities, not statistical precision.

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text:
The parent designs, procures and executes civil/electrical, industrial, civic-utility and water infrastructure, including subcontract work for principal contractors. Billing and certification precede collection; retention, advances, guarantees and materials create substantial cash commitments. At the acquired subsidiary, mining development/operations and transportation add equipment-heavy, longer-duration contracts. Equipment rental is a newer parent activity with assets already purchased but significant operating contribution still to be demonstrated. [S1][S12]

Management described Q1 FY27 group revenue of ₹378.77 crore, including roughly ₹137.64 crore mining and ₹40.76 crore transportation, versus standalone revenue ₹200.32 crore. These segment figures are attributed to management; the model uses signed parent/group totals rather than assuming a perfect entity/segment equivalence. FY24 subcontracted revenue was 78.96%, while repeat customers contributed 58.64%. Repeat work supports access but does not remove client bargaining power or principal-contractor payment risk. Current customer concentration and a fully cash-backed backlog schedule remain unavailable. [S2][S12][S16]

sections.title: 5. Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The proposed advantage is execution relationships and qualification history: successful work can lead to repeat packages and broader bidding eligibility. The evidence is repeat revenue and sustained scale-up. Durability is limited by competitive tendering, reliance on counterparties to provide work fronts and cash, and the investment needed to staff/equip larger contracts. A capable funded competitor can bid against these economics; no durable cost curve, switching lock-in, proprietary asset or independently verified market-share advantage has been established. MOAT 4 reflects contestable economics, not a penalty for SME size. [S1][S12][S16]

The IPO prospectus compares Capacit’e Infraprojects, Chavda Infra, AVP Infracon and PSP Projects. These are useful EPC execution/collection comparators, not exact matches for the newly acquired mining/transport mix. Its November 2024 peer P/Es are stale and are not imported as October 2026 fair-value multiples. The scenario 5x/7x/9x exits are analyst sensitivities, not validated peer-derived targets. Current directly comparable competitor multiples and a defined market-share denominator remain gaps. [S16]

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Standalone/predecessor revenue progressed from ₹80.24 crore in FY22 to ₹133.49 crore FY23, ₹290.34 crore FY24, ₹538.22 crore FY25 and ₹831.87 crore FY26. Annual additions were ₹53.25 crore, ₹156.85 crore, ₹247.88 crore and ₹293.65 crore. FY24 combines the partnership period ending 12 February 2024 and successor period beginning 13 February, without overlapping them. Preferred three-year FY23-FY26 CAGR is 84.02%; four-year FY22-FY26 context is 79.44%. Five- and ten-year CAGRs are ND, not invented from too few endpoints. [S1][S16]

FY26 parent growth was 54.56%. Q1 FY27 parent growth slowed to 10.88%, while reported group growth of 109.66% reflects the expanded perimeter. KTL’s balance sheet was consolidated from control on 31 March 2026 at 39.78% ownership; ownership reached 60% on 14 April. The acquisition is not proof of organic revenue acceleration. Parent June TTM sales are ₹851.53 crore using FY26 + current Q1 − prior Q1. Group reported TTM sales are ₹1,033.65 crore, explicitly non-constant-scope. No reliable volume/price/mix split or comparable earlier TTM growth is supplied. [S2][S3][S5]

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Management’s approximate ₹1,600 crore parent backlog over 18-24 months implies ₹800-1,067 crore annual execution if schedules hold, against FY26 parent sales ₹831.87 crore. The subsidiary’s approximate ₹2,400 crore six-year backlog implies roughly ₹400 crore annual execution, but that is neither a revenue guarantee nor a substitute for total mining/transport activity. Parent base FY27 revenue ₹880 crore is within that illustrative backlog pace; residual ₹720 crore relies on continued activity beyond a straight-line backlog conversion and is less firmly supported. No headline infrastructure TAM is used as proof of accessible share. [S1][S12]

The model funds new working-capital stocks, maintenance and growth capex, interest, mandatory amortization and legacy claims. Higher sales need cash, not just orders. ₹59.80 crore of FY26 parent equipment additions were on credit, and rental revenues were still expected from Q2 according to the August call. Meaningful group incremental ROIC cannot yet be isolated from acquisitions, margin expansion, debtor conversion and commissioning lags. CAP is therefore NS despite a favorable parent-only diagnostic. Persistent negative cash conversion caps any eventual GQS at 5 on current evidence. An uncommitted ₹120 crore facility is an analytical variable, not an available reinvestment runway. [S1][S9][S10][S12]

sections.title: 8. Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Vibhoar Agrawal and Rachita Agrawal are the identified promoters. The last directly reviewed annual shareholding table shows 57.73% promoter ownership at 31 March 2026; later issuance changes that denominator, so it is not presented as a verified October percentage. Piyush Kothari & Associates issued unmodified annual reports; this does not independently validate future recoverability or every related-party term. Note 30 discloses related-party loans, transactions and security deposits, including ₹18.71 crore combined deposits with two related entities. These warrant commercial-term scrutiny but do not establish abuse. [S1][S16]

Observable delivery: March board control and April rights completion are documented; July warrant allotment and August conversion raised actual cash; the Shirdi subcontract was terminated in May with a ₹76.11 crore backlog reduction because, according to the company, work fronts were unavailable. Management’s August expectation of equipment-rental revenue from Q2 and declining finance cost from Q2/Q3 remains unverified at this cutoff. Promises are not scored as delivered. [S3][S5][S6][S7][S12][S13]

The company acknowledged a quarterly-versus-half-year XBRL tagging error on 13 June and said revised filing would correct it. In its 27 August disclosure, it reported an ED search at its premises on 20 January 2026. The company said the search concerned the erstwhile partnership/other entities or persons, that no proceedings or investigation had been initiated against the company pursuant to it, and that no attachment, seizure, freezing order or other restriction continued against company assets as of that disclosure. It attributed delayed disclosure to its understanding of the event and subsequent exchange clarification. This is the company’s account, not an independently verified clearance or proof of misconduct; no contrary enforcement disposition was established in the reviewed source set. [S14][S15]

sections.title: 9. Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY26 parent PAT was ₹70.83 crore on ₹831.87 crore sales, while CFO was negative ₹41.09 crore. FY25 PAT was ₹40.05 crore and CFO negative ₹80.14 crore. Including FY24, cumulative CFO/PAT is −0.997x, calculated as a ratio of sums, not an average of annual ratios. FY26 parent cash-capex FCF proxy is −₹43.17 crore; the group proxy is −₹42.98 crore. This cash-capex proxy omits equipment purchased on credit and acquisitions, so it is not owner free cash. Interest cash payments are in financing under these statements. [S1][S16]

Parent core EBITDA, excluding other income, rose from ₹52.41 crore FY25 to ₹104.59 crore FY26. Parent core EBIT/interest was 10.51x FY26, but Q1 FY27 fell to 4.87x as finance cost rose. Q1 group core EBITDA is ₹59.72 crore from PBT + interest + depreciation − other income, not a promotional EBITDA label. FY26 group earnings include ₹5.08 crore associate profit; March liabilities include KTL at year-end control without a full year of its operating results, so March group debt/FY26 EBITDA is a mismatched-perimeter leverage ratio and is not used for a precise solvency verdict. [S1][S2]

Parent average-receivable days on total sales increased from 52.71 FY25 to 65.55 FY26, but the FY26 debtor-to-subsidiary-investment conversion of ₹51.68 crore depresses the closing debtor stock and limits comparability. The call’s roughly 100-110 group debtor days is management’s dated statement, not verified collection history. Group inventory ₹111.97 crore, receivables ₹337.48 crore and advances ₹209.02 crore are not cash. [S1][S12]

Every opening claim has one treatment in the model. ₹70.7101 crore capital-goods creditors are paid separately from ordinary WC and new capex; tax asset ₹17.4182 crore is recovered separately from WC, with forecast tax and ₹5.5672 crore opening current tax distinct. ₹0.4272 crore dividend and current provisions are paid once. Gratuity remains ₹147.13 lakh total from balance-sheet liabilities despite inconsistent note disclosures; long-term runoff is assumed, not immediate full payment. Deferred tax ₹24.9788 crore remains a terminal claim. ₹50.7149 crore FDs receive no default liquidity credit; ₹30.5470 crore noncurrent deposits remain operating assets. Salary/statutory/customer-advance/retention/other operating claims stay in the working-capital ledger, not silently erased. The parent-only FY23-FY26 diagnostic shows a ₹70.43 crore NOPAT increase over ₹216.90 crore increase in a book-funding capital proxy, or 32.47%, using 25% assumed tax. This is not reconciled group ROIC or project IRR. An illustrative 12%-16% nominal INR post-tax capital-cost range assumes 10%-13% pre-tax borrowing costs, 17%-22% equity costs and roughly balanced funding; it is not a measured issuer WACC or the separate 15% equity-return hurdle. The parent proxy clears that range arithmetically, but acquisition effects, margin expansion and unseasoned equipment capital prevent a reliable whole-group incremental-return conclusion. [S1][S16]

sections.title: 10. Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
Two methods are used without pretending they resolve funding: a dated two-pool cash/claims/terminal-return model, and a parent TTM earnings/owners-book cross-check. ₹84 implies ₹367.68 crore current market capitalization, approximately 4.99x parent June TTM PAT and 1.44x March group owners book. The latter mixes dates and is not a current liquidation value. No current group EV/EBITDA is asserted by subtracting restricted deposits or pairing March acquisition debt with a noncomparable profit year. [S1][S2][S7][S17]

The explicitly conditional FY27 revenue resets (parent/residual) are ₹880/720 crore base, ₹940/800 crore bull and ₹800/660 crore bear. Thereafter growth is 12%/10%, 18%/16% and 4%/3%, respectively; operating margins are 14.5%/17%, 16%/19% and 11.5%/13.5%; exit multiples 7x, 9x and 5x. Working capital, impairments, maintenance, incremental growth capex, interest, taxes, compulsory principal, claims, fees, warrant proceeds and rescue shares are linked by dated cash identities. Annual outputs and terminal bridges are included in the valuation audit. [S1][S2]

Conditional results: base: exit ₹474.10-₹491.93, IRR 41.36%-42.40%, rescue equity ₹3.45 crore; bull: exit ₹954.23-₹997.98, IRR 62.58%-64.05%, rescue equity ₹5.96 crore; bear: exit ₹122.81-₹123.36, IRR 7.89%-7.99%, rescue equity ₹87.82 crore. These are not expected returns. The model assumes up to ₹120 crore new facility and ₹120 crore new equity, neither proven available. Base/bull use discounted ₹67.20 rescue equity; bear ₹50.40; severe ₹33.60, with 3% equity fees. The residual’s 51%-60% attribution range is not precise KTL fair value. Actual issued shares differ from weighted-average EPS shares and from terminal scenario shares. No future dividends are included or double-counted. [S6][S7][S9][S10]

₹84 needs ₹168.95 terminal value for 15% over five years. At unchanged base cash generation the algebraic exit hurdle is about 2.44x common EV/EBITDA, but its apparently low threshold relies on modeled funding, collection and repayment. The growth solution is approximately −17.21%, driven by working-capital release and unchanged margins, not proof of resilient shrinking economics. Nine growth/margin combinations, 5x/7x/9x exits and 12%/15%/18% hurdles are disclosed; all remain conditional. There is no supported actionable entry range until financeable cash flows and attributable equity are established. R and P stay NS.

sections.title: 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest adverse chain is slower certification/collection → working-capital absorption → higher borrowing cost → cash reserved for legacy creditors and mandatory principal → refinancing or dilutive equity required. A quoted low P/E cannot protect against an unfunded cash gap. The primary severe path exhausts its finite hypothetical funding on 31 January 2027 and receives no going-concern exit value or investor IRR. Loss severity is Severe in that failure path; actual recovery cannot be estimated from illiquid carrying values. [S1][S2]

The restrained survival test begins with a common modeled bridge to 20 October, including about ₹35.47 crore unverified pre-cutoff facility use. Afterward it stops growth capex, new drawings, rescue equity, remaining warrant cash and voluntary debt sweeps; it retains maintenance, tax, old capital creditors and mandatory principal, renews existing demand debt without expansion, and uses a zero cash buffer. Flat-growth/base margins fail by ₹5.17 lakh on 30 November. Parent/residual margins 12%/14%, credible relative to historical parent margins and new acquired-business uncertainty, fail by ₹375.83 lakh in November. Lower maintenance of 0.6%/4% of revenue still leaves ₹264.53 lakh negative. Additional collection stress fails by ₹2,882.79 lakh aggregate in October; that is a more severe sensitivity, not needed to force the gate. No surviving no-rescue case was demonstrated among these four. [S1][S2]

The best counterargument is that actual October liquidity, committed lines, customer advances, settlement timing or cash collections may be better than the modeled bridge. Rated facilities and a profitable operating base support that possibility; they do not establish it. The small first deficit is timing-sensitive. Therefore these are conditional model failure dates, not reports of actual default or predictions of an insolvency date. The thesis-break variable is accessible, evidenced liquidity after unavoidable claims, not the order-book headline. [S9][S10]

sections.title: 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: A five-year 5x price outcome requires approximately 38.0% annualized price growth; 10x requires 58.5%. The conditional base and bull model outputs mechanically span such outcomes, but only after assumed funding, sustained margins, working-capital realization and terminal valuation. That arithmetic does not establish accessible demand, dilution terms or the probability of success. A lower 5x terminal multiple is separately tested, and an unfunded path has no shareholder IRR. Given low confidence in current-group incremental economics and funding, 5x/10x outcomes are Speculative / unsupported rather than an investment thesis. No precise probability or promotional price target is assigned. [S1][S2][S9][S10]

sections.title: 13. Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
Research checkpoints, not automated alerts:
1. Current liquidity: reconcile observed parent and entity cash/debt to the March ₹494.41 crore group debt and ₹11.70 crore cash. Investigate any unexplained bridge; thesis break is inability to meet an actual due claim without unapproved rescue.
2. Funding availability: obtain sanctions, undrawn amounts, covenants and renewal dates behind rated ₹196 crore parent/₹250 crore subsidiary facilities. A rating alone does not meet the milestone.
3. Cash conversion: compare subsequent CFO with certified receivable collections; two-year parent CFO is −₹121.23 crore. Continued negative CFO despite claimed collections is a warning; persistent inability to fund mandatory costs changes survival assessment.
4. Capital creditors: track the ₹70.71 crore opening obligation separately from new equipment capex. Reconcile payment terms, settlements and fresh supplier credit.
5. Rental commissioning: test the August promise of Q2 rental activity against actual recognized rental revenue, utilization, cash collection and maintenance; do not treat equipment delivery as earnings delivery.
6. KTL attribution: reconcile entity P&L, ownership and minority claims from March control to April 60%; require a cash-access and intercompany-loan schedule.
7. Warrants: 4,183,200 remain after August conversion. Any conversion must match actual cash and issued shares; expiry/nonconversion removes assumed proceeds.
8. Backlog: reconcile approximately ₹4,090 crore claimed group backlog to execution, cancellations and funded customers; use the Shirdi cancellation as evidence that booked orders can disappear.
9. Trading: refresh 20/60-session turnover, lot and restrictions before any implementation; recent conservative turnover ₹34.71 lakh is weaker than the 60-session ₹51.00 lakh baseline. [S1][S6][S7][S9][S10][S12][S13][S17][S19]

sections.title: 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Classification: Distressed / funding failure in the conditional model; Hold — unresolved for a new-investment decision because current funding and attributable returns cannot be underwritten. This is not a statement of actual issuer default. G3 excludes favorable investability; IAS remains NS, with the policy ceiling 3 disclosed rather than substituted for missing evidence. BQS and GQS remain NS because current-group CAP is unresolved, despite substantial scoreable historical evidence. All three ranking eligibility flags are false. [S1][S2][S9][S10]

Research priority is high for resolving liquidity, not a buy recommendation. No compounder designation is available: CAP is NS, CASH 2 and BAL 3 do not meet criteria. A lower price changes the investment setup but cannot itself repair an unavailable funding bridge; reliable current cash, sanctioned headroom and sustained collections could. No holdings, tax context or personal position size were supplied, so there is no portfolio exit count or trade instruction. A favorable reassessment requires verified survival and attributable cash economics, not merely a share-price rebound.

sections.title: 15. Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary source ledger: annual report [S1], Q1 signed results [S2], KTL control/rights filings [S3-S5], warrant/listing actions [S6-S8], parent/subsidiary bank and NCD ratings [S9-S11], management call [S12], Shirdi termination [S13], XBRL response [S14], legal-event disclosure with company response [S15], pre-IPO prospectus [S16], and official market/security/surveillance files [S17-S19]. Each ledger entry supplies exact URL, date, scope, locators, confidence and limitations. Sources were read selectively for material claims rather than treating every page as independently verified.

Key assumptions: forecast margins/growth, working-capital recovery, 25.17% forecast earnings tax (25% only in the separate parent capital diagnostic), maintenance rates, settlement schedules, full parent support of residual shortfalls, hypothetical funding and discounted rescue equity, no future dividends, terminal multiples, no FD liquidity credit and 51%-60% residual attribution. Five-year return = (terminal price/84)^(1/5)−1. Missing-data score bounds use original weights without redistribution. The weights are research conventions, not validated return predictors.

Open questions: current observed cash and debt; sanctions/headroom/renewal commitments; complete entity debt, guarantees and restrictions; asset collectibility and tax refunds; exact maturity/creditor settlement schedules; group incremental capital economics and current minority attribution; current customer/supplier concentration; complete backlog/cancellation bridge; exact final IPO use-of-proceeds reconciliation; updated promoter encumbrances; unresolved gratuity-note reconciliation; and current live liquidity. RHP cash-flow narrative discrepancies are resolved for the historical table using the signed annexure; other granular legacy capital differences are not forced into precise group ROIC. None of these gaps authorizes an allegation or a neutral placeholder score.

monitoring_plan.checkpoints:
Research checkpoints, not automated alerts:
1. Current liquidity: reconcile observed parent and entity cash/debt to the March ₹494.41 crore group debt and ₹11.70 crore cash. Investigate any unexplained bridge; thesis break is inability to meet an actual due claim without unapproved rescue.
2. Funding availability: obtain sanctions, undrawn amounts, covenants and renewal dates behind rated ₹196 crore parent/₹250 crore subsidiary facilities. A rating alone does not meet the milestone.
3. Cash conversion: compare subsequent CFO with certified receivable collections; two-year parent CFO is −₹121.23 crore. Continued negative CFO despite claimed collections is a warning; persistent inability to fund mandatory costs changes survival assessment.
4. Capital creditors: track the ₹70.71 crore opening obligation separately from new equipment capex. Reconcile payment terms, settlements and fresh supplier credit.
5. Rental commissioning: test the August promise of Q2 rental activity against actual recognized rental revenue, utilization, cash collection and maintenance; do not treat equipment delivery as earnings delivery.
6. KTL attribution: reconcile entity P&L, ownership and minority claims from March control to April 60%; require a cash-access and intercompany-loan schedule.
7. Warrants: 4,183,200 remain after August conversion. Any conversion must match actual cash and issued shares; expiry/nonconversion removes assumed proceeds.
8. Backlog: reconcile approximately ₹4,090 crore claimed group backlog to execution, cancellations and funded customers; use the Shirdi cancellation as evidence that booked orders can disappear.
9. Trading: refresh 20/60-session turnover, lot and restrictions before any implementation; recent conservative turnover ₹34.71 lakh is weaker than the 60-session ₹51.00 lakh baseline. [S1][S6][S7][S9][S10][S12][S13][S17][S19]
monitoring_plan.cadence: At next signed results/capital action and before any implementation; research recommendation only.

limitations: Observed October cash, debt, restricted balances and accessible entity liquidity are unavailable; the common bridge is modeled.
Available sanctioned undrawn funding, covenant headroom and demand-debt renewal commitments are not proved by ratings.
Current-group incremental IC/returns and attributable subsidiary economics remain unresolved after acquisition; CAP, R and P are NS.
Timing of mandatory principal, capital creditors and tax recovery is modeled rather than contract-verified month by month.
Whole-group guarantees/contingencies, FD restrictions and intercompany cash mobility are incompletely established.
Gratuity-note conflict remains: retain balance-sheet liabilities totaling ₹147.13 lakh, not an unsupported replacement.
No current full customer/supplier concentration, reconciled backlog roll-forward or complete IPO use-of-proceeds reconciliation.
Latest reviewed promoter holding is March 2026; a current full encumbrance history is unavailable.
Legacy prospectus narrative cash-flow conflicts require signed-annexure preference; current group is not a comparable historical perimeter.
No live spread/depth; historical liquidity and EOD restrictions are not guaranteed execution.
ED-event status is based on the dated company response; no independently verified enforcement disposition or proven misconduct established.
next_steps: Verify observed October liquidity and committed renewal/drawability before underwriting any return.
Reconcile entity-level capital employed, minority claims, intercompany advances and contract cash timing.
Check rental commissioning, collections, signed use-of-proceeds and subsequent capital conversion disclosures.
